'''Stephen L. Buchwald''' (born 1955) is an American chemist and the [[Camille Dreyfus (chemist)|Camille Dreyfus]] Professor of Chemistry at [[MIT]]. He is known for his involvement in the development of the [[Buchwald-Hartwig amination]]<ref>{{cite book | last=Tsuji | first=J. | date=November 23, 1999 | title=Perspectives in Organopalladium Chemistry for the 21st Century | publisher=[[Elsevier|Elsevier Science]] | page=125 | isbn=0-444-50197-5}}</ref> and the discovery of the [[Dialkylbiaryl Phosphine Ligands|dialkylbiaryl phosphine]] ligand family for promoting this reaction and related transformations. He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and as a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2000 and 2008, respectively.

==Early life and education==
Stephen Buchwald was born in [[Bloomington, Indiana]]. He credits his "young and dynamic" high school chemistry teacher, William Lumbley, for infecting him with his enthusiasm.<ref name=bbva>[https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/galardonado/stephen-buchwald-2/ Stephen Buchwald. Frontiers of Knowledge LAUREATE] BBVA Foundation, n.d., retrieved July 2, 2018</ref>

In 1977 he received his [[Sc.B.]] from [[Brown University]] where he worked with Kathlyn A. Parker and [[David E. Cane]] as well as [[Gilbert Stork]] from [[Columbia University]]. In 1982 he received his Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]] working under [[Jeremy R. Knowles]].<ref name=MITpersonalpage>{{cite web|title=About Steve|url=http://chemistry-buchwald.mit.edu/stephen-buchwald|publisher=MIT|accessdate=August 10, 2015|date=n.d.}}</ref>

==Career==
Buchwald was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Caltech]] with [[Robert H. Grubbs]]. In 1984, he joined [[MIT faculty]] as an assistant professor of chemistry. He was promoted to associate professor in 1989 and to Professor in 1993. He was named the Camille Dreyfus Professor in 1997. He has coauthored over 435 accepted [[academic publications]] and 47 accepted patents.<ref name=MITpersonalpage/>

He is known for his involvement in the development of the [[Buchwald-Hartwig amination]] and the discovery of the [[Dialkylbiaryl Phosphine Ligands|dialkylbiaryl phosphine]] ligand family for promoting this reaction and related transformations. He was elected as a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and as a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2000 and 2008, respectively.<ref name=MITpersonalpage/> 
{{As of| 2015}}, he served as an associate editor for the academic journal, ''[[Advanced Synthesis & Catalysis]]''.<ref name="Hickman 2014">{{cite web | last=Hickman | first=Daniel | title=Buchwald Receives 2014 Linus Pauling Medal | website=ChemistryViews | date=October 11, 2014 | url=https://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/6831201/Buchwald_Receives_2014_Linus_Pauling_Medal/ | access-date=August 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Advanced Synthesis & Catalysis, Editorial Board|url=http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/10.1002/(ISSN)1615-4169/homepage/2258_edbd.html|journal=Advanced Synthesis & Catalysis|accessdate=August 10, 2015|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1615-4169|s2cid=251017690 |doi-access=|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Notable awards==
Awards received by Buchwald include:<ref name=MITpersonalpage/>
* 2005 - [[Chemical Abstract Services|CAS]] Science Spotlight Award
* 2005 - [[Bristol-Myers Squibb]] Distinguished Achievement Award
* 2006 – [[American Chemical Society]] Award for Creative Work in Synthetic Organic Chemistry
* 2006 – Siegfried Medal Award in Chemical Methods which Impact Process Chemistry
* 2010 – Gustavus J. Esselen Award for Chemistry in the Public Interest
* 2013 – [[Arthur C. Cope Award]]
* 2014 – Ulysses Medal, [[University College Dublin]]
* 2014 – [[Linus Pauling Award]]<ref name=linusmedalnews>{{cite web|title=Buchwald Receives 2014 Linus Pauling Medal|url=http://www.chemistryviews.org/details/ezine/6831201/Buchwald_Receives_2014_Linus_Pauling_Medal.html|website=Chemistry Views|date=October 11, 2014 |publisher=Wiley-VCH Verlag GmbH & Co. KGaA, Weinheim|accessdate=August 10, 2015}}</ref>
* 2014 – [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in Basic Sciences <ref>[https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/version/edition_2014/ BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award 2014]</ref>
* 2015 – honorary doctorate, [[University of South Florida]]
* 2016 – [[William H. Nichols Medal]]
* 2019 – [[Wolf Prize in Chemistry]]<ref>[https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Wolf-Prize-laureates-announced-577584 Wolf Prize 2019 – Jerusalem Post]</ref>
* 2019 – Roger Adams Award, [[American Chemical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=The 2019 Adams Award goes to Professor Buchwald |url=https://www.organicdivision.org/blog/2018/09/16/the-2019-adams-award-goes-to-professor-buchwald/ |website=ACS Division of Organic Chemistry |accessdate=July 15, 2019 |date=September 16, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Video: Presentation of the Adams Award to Professor Buchwald at the 2019 National Organic Chemistry Symposium|url=https://www.organicdivision.org/nos2019rogeradamsawardpresentation/ |website=ACS Division of Organic Chemistry |accessdate=July 15, 2019 |date=July 15, 2019}}</ref>
* 2020 – [[Clarivate Citation Laureates|Clarivate Citation Laureate]]
